subject: Data retention variance & PII handling — next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Park <lauren@finservco.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.ops@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: retention & PII ask from today

Hi Monica — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks from our security/legal side so we can move this forward: 

- FinServCo must not persist any request or response payloads containing customer PII (names, SSNs, account numbers). We would prefer a 0-retention policy for payloads.
- Application/team OK with short operational logs for debugging, but retention must be 7 days max and exclude text payloads.
- Audit trail (who/when) is required but must be redacted and exported to our SIEM within 24 hours.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can support a hard 0-retention option for payloads and the 7-day operational logs constraint? If not, what alternatives would you propose?

I've attached our compliance note (data-retention-exception-request.pdf). Please loop in engineering/security as needed.

Thanks,
Lauren Park
Head of Product — FinServCo
lauren@finservco.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@finservco.com>

Date: 2026-04-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: retention & PII ask from today

Hi Lauren — great talking today, appreciate the clear asks. Short recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap: FinServCo requires 0-retention for PII payloads (preference), 7-day max for operational logs (no text payloads), and redacted audit exports to SIEM within 24h.

What we can offer (high level):
- Zero-persist option for request/response payloads at the API layer (no long-term storage of content).
- Short-term operational logs configurable per-customer (default 7 days) with redaction rules to remove free-text.
- Export hooks to push audit events to your SIEM within 24h.
- If stricter controls are required, Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment gives you control and contractual guarantees + KMS integration.

Next steps: 
1) Karthik and Vivek from our infra/security team to confirm the technical details and constraints (I’ve cc’d them).
2) I’ll send a proposed retention schedule and a draft MSA clause for the exception.
3) Optional: short technical deep-dive next week to validate non-persistence and SIEM export.

Attaching: redwood-soc2-brief.pdf (SOC2 overview) — Karthik/Vivek, please review Lauren’s attachment and flag anything we can’t meet.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Monica/Karthik — thanks. A few contract-level items we want to confirm up front before a pilot: 

- We require a contractual warranty that request/response payloads containing PII will not be stored persistently by Redwood (0-retention).
- Operational logs for troubleshooting may exist but must not contain full payloads or customer PII; retention = 7 days.
- KV/cache must be ephemeral and not persisted beyond the processing window.
- Any backups that might contain payload data must be excluded or encrypted with our KMS and accessible only on-demand for audits.

If Redwood cannot provide strict 0-retention, please provide the shortest feasible retention and the technical controls that enforce that retention (e.g., auto-delete hooks, write-once ephemeral buffers, logging filters). We’ll then assess whether a legal exception is feasible.

Evelyn Cho
Senior Counsel, FinServCo
evelyn.legal@finservco.com
(Attachment: data-retention-exception-request.pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Cho <evelyn.legal@finservco.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Tom Alvarez <tom.ops@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-04-14T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: retention & PII ask from today

Evelyn — thanks for the specifics. Technical clarifications from infra/security (conservative summary):

- Zero-persist (payloads): We support an API-level configuration that does not write request/response payloads to durable storage (no DB or object-store writes). In hosted mode we still generate short-lived in-memory buffers and transient metrics; these are deleted immediately after processing. For cryptographic guarantees and full audit separation, Dedicated/Private deployment is recommended.

- Operational logs: We can enforce log redaction filters so logs exclude free-text payloads and PII fields. Retention windows are configurable; we can set 7 days for your account.

- KV cache behavior: We can enable an ephemeral-only KV cache mode (in-memory, no checkpointing). Note that for certain model performance features (large context windows) this will increase latency but meets the non-persistence requirement.

- Backups & snapshots: Hosted backups are not meant to contain customer payloads if zero-persist is enabled, but we will provide a documented guarantee and controls. For additional assurance, we can integrate with your KMS for encryption-at-rest or run a Private deployment where you control keys.

Proposed compromise (practical option):
1) Pilot on Dedicated capacity with zero-persist payload config + in-memory ephemeral KV cache.
2) Operational logs redacted and retained 7 days.
3) Audit events exported to your SIEM within 24h (we’ll provide S3/HTTPS delivery).

I attached a short retention proposal spreadsheet (retention-proposal-20260414.xlsx) that maps controls to contract language and the expected impact on features/latency. If this looks acceptable, we’ll produce a redline for the MSA and schedule a technical deep-dive.

- Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Lauren/Evelyn — thanks and appreciate the detail. Quick summary and action items to get to a pilot: 

Summary: Karthik confirmed a zero-persist option at the API layer (hosted with constraints) and recommends Dedicated/Private for strongest guarantees. Operational logs can be redacted and held for 7 days; audit exports available within 24h. KV cache can be configured ephemeral-only (tradeoff: higher latency).

Action items: 
- Monica (Redwood): Prepare MSA redline language for the 0-retention clause and share by 2026-04-16 EOD. (attachment: retention-proposal-20260414.xlsx)
- Karthik/Vivek: Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with FinServCo ops/security next week (prefer Wed/Thu).
- FinServCo: Confirm whether Dedicated/Private is required or if hosted zero-persist is an acceptable pilot approach.

If we can align on pilot scope (Dedicated or hosted-zero-persist), I’ll create the mutual action plan and pull legal in for redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly here.

Best,
